title: Question 1
stem: A planet has mass $M = 2.55 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}$ and radius $R = 6.05 \times 10^6\text{ m}$. A satellite is in a circular orbit about the planet.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define gravitational potential at a point.

markscheme_points.text: in bringing a point mass from infinity to the point

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the gravitational field strength $g$ at the surface of the planet is $4.65\text{ N kg}^{-1}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in gravitational potential connecting them.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Gravitational potential. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$g = GM / R^2 = (6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 2.55 \times 10^{24}) / (6.05 \times 10^6)^2 = 4.65\text{ N kg}^{-1}$
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Show that the orbital period $T$ of the satellite is $18\text{ hours}$.

markscheme_points.text: $GMm / r^2 = m v^2 / r$ and $v = 2\pi r / T$ (or $GMm / r^2 = m r \omega^2$ and $\omega = 2\pi / T$)

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in gravitational potential connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
Hint 4: Clearly show every intermediate algebraic substitution and ensure your final value has correct physical units.
parts.proper_answer: $GMm / r^2 = m v^2 / r$ and $v = 2\pi r / T$ (or $GMm / r^2 = m r \omega^2$ and $\omega = 2\pi / T$); $T^2 = 4\pi^2 r^3 / (GM) = (4\pi^2 \times (2.65 \times 10^7)^3) / (6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 2.55 \times 10^{24}) = 4.20 \times 10^9$; $T = \sqrt{4.20 \times 10^9} = 64800\text{ s}$; $T = 64800 / 3600 = 18\text{ hours}$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State one similarity and one difference between gravitational potential and electric potential.

markscheme_points.text: similarity: both are inversely proportional to distance from point mass/charge (or zero at infinity / spherical equipotentials)
difference: gravitational potential is always negative (attractive), whereas electric potential can be positive or negative
